newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil studies ways to cut cost of export finance.
newsitem.headline: Brazil studies ways to cut cost of export finance.

text.p: The Brazilian government is studying ways to reduce the cost of export finance and expects measures already taken or being mulled will boost exports next year, a Ministry of Industry and Commerce official said.

Acknowledging October would post a deficit and exports by year-end should show lower-than-expected growth of some 4.5 percent, foreign trade secretary Mauricio Cortes said Brasilia was seeking greater flexibility and lower capitalization costs for exporters.
"All these things will have an effect on exports next year," Cortes told reporters.

Cortes said the National Development Bank (BNDES) was studying export finance costs and the government itself had taken on the task of slashing back the cost of doing business in Brazil, the so-called "Brazil Cost."
He said a recently-recreated export insurance plan would "open new horizons" for exporters and in addition, expectations of a larger harvest in 1997 would raise shipments and lower imports next year.
Cortes said October would post a trade deficit, but he declined to estimate its size or comment on speculation the gap could reach $1.0 billion or more.

Questioned about export growth this year, he acknowledged that predictions of an increase of around 4.5 percent over 1995's total exports of $40.304 was reasonable. Initial government estimates were of 7.0-8.0 percent growth.
